name: protobufjs-cli (protoc substitute)
build_opts: npm lane: resolve+fetch+bundle `protobufjs-cli@2.5.4` (+ peer `protobufjs@^8.6.3`); deps all pure-JS (chalk, escodegen, espree, estraverse, glob, jsdoc, minimist, tmp) — NO gypfile/postinstall/node-gyp/native addons (verified registry manifest). Entry: bin pbjs (proto->JSON/static-JS/descriptor) and pbts (.d.ts). Run resulting bundle on QuickJS with JsDock Node fs/path shims (already live). bundlejob.js / compilers/js lane, no per-tool host work.
smoke: echo 'syntax="proto3"; message M { int32 id = 1; string name = 2; }' > a.proto; pbjs -t json a.proto  ->  expect JSON with nested.M.fields.id.type=int32, .name.type=string. Also pbjs -t static-module a.proto emits a JS encoder/decoder module.
blocker: protoc itself (C++) has NO plain wasm32-wasi build (emscripten/js-pair only) and needs a bootstrap-protoc codegen step + abseil + CMake configure -> lanes A/B/C dead. protobufjs-cli is the pure-JS equivalent reached via lane D. Residual risk: pbts path pulls heavy `jsdoc`; if jsdoc trips a Node API the fs shim lacks, pbts (.d.ts gen) may degrade while core pbjs (.proto->JSON/JS) still works — not a build blocker, only a feature-surface caveat.

name: flatc
build_opts: deps=[github:google/flatbuffers @ main tarball]; src_globs=[src/*.cpp, src/util.cpp, src/file_manager.cpp, src/file_name_manager.cpp, src/idl_parser.cpp, src/reflection.cpp, src/code_generators.cpp, src/binary_annotator.cpp, src/annotated_binary_text_gen.cpp, src/bfbs_gen_lua.cpp, src/bfbs_gen_nim.cpp, src/idl_gen_*.cpp, src/flatc.cpp, src/flatc_main.cpp, include/codegen/python.cc, grpc/src/compiler/*_generator.cc]; exclude=[tests/**, grpc/tests/**, src/idl_gen_lua.* (none), samples/**]; compile_only=[all above]; main=src/flatc_main.cpp; cflags=[-std=c++17, -Iinclude, -Igrpc, -fno-exceptions (flatc core throws no C++ exceptions; 'throw' tokens are only inside emitted-code string literals), -O2, --target=wasm32-wasi, -D_WASI_EMULATED_SIGNAL maybe]; libc++ (clang+libc++ amalgam lane). No configure_file C++ config header needed; reflection_generated.h is checked in; parser hand-written (no flex/bison).
smoke: echo 'table T{a:int;} root_type T;' > t.fbs && flatc --cpp t.fbs && test -f t_generated.h && echo OK
blocker: none — fixed file list is hand-enumerable (globs+excludes), no configure/codegen tool runs to build the flatc binary itself. Only nuance: must include grpc/src/compiler/*_generator.cc + include/codegen/python.cc because idl_gen_grpc.cpp/idl_gen_python.cpp reference them; this is enumeration, not configure-time discovery.

name: csvkit
build_opts: Lane D (pure-Python, CPython/Pyodide-on-wasm). Vendor site-packages: pip install --target=<sysroot>/site-packages csvkit==2.2.0 (resolves full pure-Python tree). Wheels: csvkit-2.2.0-py3-none-any, agate-1.14.2-py3-none-any, agate_excel-0.4.2, agate_dbf-0.2.4, agate_sql-0.7.3, openpyxl-3.1.5-py2.py3-none-any, xlrd-2.0.2, python_slugify-8.0.4, leather-0.4.1, parsedatetime, pytimeparse2, Babel, et_xmlfile, dbfread, greenlet(optional-skip), sqlalchemy-2.0.50 (use py3-none-any fallback wheel; C-ext optional). No native C-ext at runtime. Entry points: csvlook/csvcut/csvstat/in2csv/csvsql/csvgrep/csvjson etc. via console_scripts.
smoke:
printf 'a,b
1,2
3,4
' | python -m csvkit.utilities.csvcut -c 1   # or: csvcut -c 1 input.csv ; csvstat input.csv ; echo expect column-a values 1,3
blocker: none — entire dep tree is pure-Python (py3-none-any wheels). Only nuance: SQLAlchemy ships cp-specific accelerator wheels but also a py3-none-any fallback; pin/select the pure wheel. greenlet (SQLAlchemy async extra) is C and unneeded for csvkit's sync use — exclude it.

name: pdftk
build_opts: JS bundle on QuickJS/esbuild lane. npm pkg: pdf-lib@1.17.1. deps (all pure-JS, no C-ext): @pdf-lib/standard-fonts, @pdf-lib/upng, pako, tslib. esbuild bundle entry wrapping pdf-lib API (merge/split/stamp/rotate/fill-form/decrypt) -> single .js, run on qjs. No native, no codegen, no configure.
smoke: qjs bundle.js: load 2 input PDFs via PDFDocument.load, mergeDocuments, save() -> assert output bytes start with %PDF and page count == sum of inputs; also rotate page 0 by 90 and re-save without error.
blocker: pdftk itself is impossible (pdftk-java = JVM; original = C++/GCJ native, no plain wasm32-wasi). Capability is delivered instead via pdf-lib on the JS lane — covers merge/split/stamp/rotate/form-fill. Note: lacks pdftk's full uncompress/repair/burst PDF-internals parity, but covers the common verbs.

name: hatchling
build_opts: lane D pure-python: pip download hatchling==1.30.1 + deps (packaging>=24.2, pathspec>=0.10.1, pluggy>=1.0.0, trove-classifiers; tomli on py<3.11) all py3-none-any wheels; unzip into site-packages on already-live CPython wasm32-wasi. No C-ext, no compile step.
smoke: python -c "import hatchling, hatchling.build as b; print(b.get_requires_for_build_wheel())" then build a wheel for a trivial pyproject (build-backend=hatchling.build) and confirm the .whl is produced.
blocker: none — pure-python build backend; only the build-backend half (hatchling), not the full hatch CLI.

name: sox
build_opts: target=libsox (the library; skip the sox.c CLI driver which needs termios/glob/signals). src=src/ with an EXPLICIT literal list (no configure, no codegen). compile_only (core, all unconditional): adpcms.c aiff.c cvsd.c g711.c g721.c g723_24.c g723_40.c g72x.c vox.c raw.c formats.c formats_i.c skelform.c xmalloc.c getopt.c util.c libsox.c libsox_i.c sox-fmt.c; effects: bend.c biquad.c biquads.c chorus.c compand.c compandt.c contrast.c dcshift.c delay.c dft_filter.c dither.c divide.c downsample.c earwax.c echo.c echos.c effects.c effects_i.c effects_i_dsp.c fade.c fft4g.c fir.c firfit.c flanger.c gain.c hilbert.c input.c ladspa.c loudness.c mcompand.c noiseprof.c noisered.c output.c overdrive.c pad.c phaser.c rate.c remix.c repeat.c reverb.c reverse.c silence.c sinc.c skeleff.c speed.c splice.c stat.c stats.c stretch.c swap.c synth.c tempo.c tremolo.c trim.c upsample.c vad.c vol.c; formats: raw-fmt.c s1-fmt.c s2-fmt.c s3-fmt.c s4-fmt.c u1-fmt.c u2-fmt.c u3-fmt.c u4-fmt.c al-fmt.c la-fmt.c ul-fmt.c lu-fmt.c 8svx.c aiff-fmt.c aifc-fmt.c au.c avr.c cdr.c cvsd-fmt.c dvms-fmt.c dat.c hcom.c htk.c maud.c prc.c sf.c smp.c sounder.c soundtool.c sphere.c tx16w.c voc.c vox-fmt.c ima-fmt.c adpcm.c ima_rw.c wav.c wve.c xa.c nulfile.c f4-fmt.c f8-fmt.c gsrt.c. EXCLUDE: sox.c, example*.c, sox_sample_test.c, *coreaudio.c, alsa.c, ao.c, pulseaudio*, sndio.c, sunaudio.c, oss*, waveaudio*, flac.c, sndfile.c, mp3.c, opus*, vorbis*, wavpack.c, amr*.c, spectrogram.c (needs PNG), win32-*. deps (in-tree, built-in, no external libs): libgsm/*.c (for gsm format) + lpc10/*.c (for lpc10 format) — both plain-C amalgams already vendored in the tarball; add their .c globs as :compile_only too, with -Ilibgsm -Ilpc10 and define EXTERNAL_GSM/EXTERNAL_LPC10 UNSET. config: hand-write src/soxconfig.h (all #undef except HAVE_STDINT_H/STRING_H/STRINGS_H/UNISTD_H/FCNTL_H/INTTYPES_H/SYS_TYPES_H/SYS_STAT_H/VSNPRINTF/STRCASECMP/STRDUP/STDC_HEADERS=1 and PACKAGE_VERSION="14.4.2"); leave HAVE_LIBLTDL/HAVE_POPEN/all codec HAVE_* undefined so only built-in formats/effects register. sox.h ships pre-generated (version 14.4.2 baked, SOX_LIB_VERSION_CODE present) — do not regenerate. cflags: -I src -I src/libgsm -I src/lpc10 -DNDEBUG -DHAVE_CONFIG_H -Wno-incompatible-function-pointer-types -Wno-format -fno-strict-aliasing. extra_sources_main=none (library target; expose lsx/sox_* entrypoints, drive via a tiny wasm shim calling sox_init/sox_open_read/sox_open_write/effects chain).
smoke: curl -fsIL the 14.4.2 tarball -> HTTP 200, 1134299 bytes (verified). Extracted; libsox source list is an EXPLICIT literal enumeration in src/Makefile.am (no glob/codegen needed). Wrote a hand-made src/soxconfig.h (all-#undef template, only POSIX HAVE_*_H + STDC set) and ran clang -fsyntax-only on representative core sources targeting host clang: wav.c, effects.c, formats.c, reverb.c all parse CLEAN (warnings only). au.c throws one incompatible-function-pointer-types diagnostic from the uint64_t-vs-long seek typedef — cosmetic, cleared by -Wno-incompatible-function-pointer-types (SoX ships these suppressed). No configure run, no flex/bison/m4/autoheader needed; sox.h + soxconfig.h.in confirm config is pure preprocessor substitution. No unconditional fork/exec/popen/system anywhere in libsox (grep clean); all process/dlopen paths gated behind HAVE_LIBLTDL/HAVE_POPEN which stay undefined.
blocker: None structural. Two minor, lane-handled items: (1) the sox CLI driver (sox.c) is NOT buildable (termios/glob/signal/realtime-audio) — build the LIBRARY (libsox) + a thin wasm shim instead, which is the right artifact anyway; (2) the LP64-vs-ILP32 seek function-pointer typedef mismatch needs -Wno-incompatible-function-pointer-types. Neither needs per-tool host work.

name: @marko/compiler
build_opts: JS bundle on QuickJS via npm-resolve+bundle. Entry: @marko/compiler (dist/index.js). Full pure-JS import graph; resolver follows actual require() calls (not just package.json deps) so it pulls @babel/core@7.x + @babel/parser/generator/traverse/types + htmljs-parser, he, jsesc, kleur, raptor-util/regexp, complain, resolve-from, self-closing-tags, source-map-support. All verified pure JS: gypfile=null, no install scripts, no node-gyp, no native addons on any node in the graph. API: compiler.compileSync(src, filename, config) -> {code}. No emscripten, no native binary.
smoke:
const {compileSync}=require('@marko/compiler'); const out=compileSync('
${input.name}
','test.marko',{output:'source'}); expect typeof out.code==='string' && out.code.length>0
blocker: None fundamental. Risk is QuickJS fidelity for a Babel-scale bundle (large graph; @babel/core uses some dynamic plugin resolution + does fs reads for browserslist/config that must be stubbed/disabled via output:'source' + explicit babelConfig to avoid filesystem lookups). Not a host-per-tool task — handled by the generic JS-bundle lane's shims, same as other Babel-family bundles.

name: @enhance/ssr
build_opts: JS bundle lane (esbuild --bundle --format=esm/iife --platform=browser) on QuickJS. entry: index.mjs. npm deps: @enhance/ssr@4.0.3, @begin/parse5@0.0.4 (bundles parse5@7, --no-builtins), nanoid@^4 (resolve random-browser.js via browser export condition to avoid node:crypto). No node fs/net needed for the render core. QuickJS crypto.getRandomValues shim covers nanoid; or pin esbuild conditions=browser.
smoke: import enhance from bundle; render an HTML string containing a registered custom element template with slots; assert expanded/composed HTML output (slot fill + attribute pass-through) matches expected — pure string-in/string-out, no DOM, no network.
blocker: none — pure-JS ESM; only nanoid touches randomness (resolved via browser crypto.getRandomValues shim / esbuild browser condition). parse5 explicitly opts out of node builtins.

name: porffor
build_opts: lane=D (JS-on-QuickJS bundle, NOT wasm32-wasi). entry=compiler/index.js (the compile API; do NOT use runtime/index.js — that's the Node CLI/REPL). pure-ESM, type=module. runtime deps: acorn (https://registry.npmjs.org/acorn/-/, pure JS, dist/acorn.mjs, zero deps, no gyp/install). node-repl-polyfill is REPL-only — exclude. Bundle: porffor compiler/*.js + builtins_precompiled.js (1.9M, SHIPPED in tarball, the precompiled stdlib — no codegen needed) + acorn into one qjs script. Shims: (1) parse.js L20 does import((globalThis.document?'https://esm.sh/':'')+parser) — no document in qjs → resolves bare 'acorn'; pre-bundle acorn so the dynamic import hits the bundled module. (2) fs/child_process/execSync are conditionally imported behind `typeof process?.version !== 'undefined'` and used ONLY for debug/disassemble/2c output — shim process={version:undefined, stdout:{write:print}} so the fs/execSync branches stay undefined and the pure compile path runs. API: default(source) -> {wasm: Uint8Array, exports, ...}; emit wasm bytes (assemble.js, pure-JS LEB128 via encoding.js, no Buffer/fs).
smoke: In qjs: load bundle, call porffor('export default () => 40 + 2') and assert the returned object has a non-empty wasm Uint8Array starting with the WASM magic (0x00 0x61 0x73 0x6d); optionally instantiate that wasm with our wasmtime/wasm host and call the export to get 42.
blocker: none for the compile-to-wasm-bytes path. Caveats (not blockers): set process.version=undefined so the node fs/child_process branches stay dormant — the -c (C output via 2c.js) and disassemble/debug paths assume Node and are out of scope; only the wasm-bytes path is in-scope. acorn dynamic import must be pre-resolved in the bundle.

name: git
build_opts: deps: [libgit2 v1.7.2 tarball]. src_globs: src/libgit2/**/*.c, src/util/**/*.c, deps/xdiff/*.c, deps/llhttp/*.c, deps/pcre/*.c, deps/zlib/*.c. exclude: src/util/win32/**, src/libgit2/win32/**, src/util/hash/openssl.c, src/util/hash/mbedtls.c, src/util/hash/win32.c, src/util/hash/common_crypto.c, **/sha1dc/** (keep builtin sha via deps/zlib or src/util/hash/builtin.c — pick exactly one sha backend), src/cli/** (skip the CLI git binary first; build lib then add a single src/cli main). cflags: --target=wasm32-wasi --sysroot=$SYSROOT -DLIBGIT2_NO_FEATURES_H -DGIT_ARCH_32_or_64 -DGIT_THREADS=0 -DGIT_HTTPS=0 -DGIT_SSH=0 -DGIT_USE_NSEC=0 -DGIT_REGEX_BUILTIN=1 -DGIT_SHA1_BUILTIN=1 -DGIT_SHA256_BUILTIN=1 -DGIT_IO_POLL=0 -DGIT_IO_SELECT=0 -Isrc/util -Isrc/libgit2 -Iinclude -Ideps/xdiff -Ideps/llhttp -Ideps/pcre -Ideps/zlib -DNO_VIZ -DSTDC. extra_sources main: thin src/cli/cli.c (git CLI entrypoint) compiled last and linked against the lib objects. Hand-write include/git2_features.h-equivalent via -D set above (NO_FEATURES_H path); disable threads/tls/ssh/http-network features that need sockets.
smoke: echo files into a tmp dir; run: git init /tmp/r && git add . && git commit -m x && git log --oneline (local object/refs ops only — no network clone/fetch).
blocker: Network transports (clone/fetch/push over http/ssh) are unreachable in-sandbox: no sockets/TLS — those subcommands compile out (GIT_HTTPS=0/GIT_SSH=0). Threads disabled (GIT_THREADS=0). Must pick exactly ONE sha1/sha256 backend (builtin) and exclude the rest, and exclude all win32/ + openssl/mbedtls/commoncrypto hash sources or you get duplicate symbols / missing headers. The bundled CLI (src/cli) is secondary — build the library first, then a thin main; if CLI source-list proves fiddly, the libgit2 library itself is the live-buildable artifact.
